text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Kabariti apologises to parliamentary deputy Amareen; parliament throws out Amareen's resignation in case marked by political and national chivalry.
- King Hussein tells Libyan leader Gaddafi the charges behind sanctions on Libya are unfair; Jordan supports easing of suffering of Libyan people.
- Jordan University students in peaceful protest against rising education costs. Higher Education Minister Ensour says no increase in baccalaureate fees.
- Crown Prince Hassan travels to Netherlands and Britain to attend global meeting on changes in world.
- Kabariti discussed with Iraqi Trade Minister Saleh details and ways of implementing U.N. Security Council Resolution 986.
- Ministry of Trade and Industry completes preparation of draft law encouraging competition and banning monopolies.

- Government moves to guarantee Jordan's share of Iraqi market. Kabariti to have another meeting with Iraqi Trade Minister Saleh on Sunday; Information Minister Muasher says no country has fixed quota of trade with Iraq -- companies should present competitive bids for business.
- Palestinian Legislative Council speaker Ahmed Korei holds talks with Kabariti; says it is up to Israel to say now if it wants treaty implemented or not.
